title: Evolve the existing Admin boundaries for controlled content sources, durable clockin tasks and a native modular UI
context: At upstream main commit 924e9d5 the Admin already has FastAPI routes and services, SQLite Task persistence primitives, a sidebar Hash-routed SPA with drawers, and single-process Docker Compose. However, third-party content providers remain hard-coded, several provider choices are dead or unsafe to follow without address validation, TaskService is not connected to clockin orchestration, active progress is memory-only, Worker responses and version 1.0 exports expose secrets, and the browser is a Tailwind/DaisyUI CDN page with one monolithic script. The approved redesign must reuse rather than duplicate working boundaries, preserve the external Worker clockin contract and exclude all ai.cqzuxia.com platform behavior.

known_evidence.summary: Validated module, dependency, public contract and rollback evidence for upstream main 924e9d5.
The baseline already contains Task and WorkerApi models but no ContentSource model.
The baseline already contains a sidebar, Hash navigation and drawers but loads Tailwind and DaisyUI from CDN.
cenguigui returned HTTP 400, the old Yuanmeng endpoint reported shutdown, KLapi and bing.img.run failed TLS, while QZQI and official Bing UHD were reachable.

options.name: Evolve existing boundaries with controlled database adapters
options.summary: Add ContentSource persistence and a dedicated content service, extend the existing Task model/service into one orchestrator, add thin APIs, and replace the current browser assets with native ES modules.
tradeoffs: Changes schema and internal Admin APIs across several modules
Reuses the current FastAPI, service, AsyncSession, scheduler and Worker boundaries
Allows provider replacement without deployment while preventing arbitrary request definitions

options.name: Patch hard-coded provider URLs and current page
options.summary: Replace dead URLs and restyle the existing monolithic Tailwind/DaisyUI page.
tradeoffs: Does not provide provider management, durable progress, secure fallback or the approved modular redesign

options.name: Introduce a frontend framework and external queue
options.summary: Use a framework build chain and a separate durable job system.
tradeoffs: Provides mature component and queue ecosystems
Adds dependencies, services and operational cost unjustified for one administrator and fewer than 50 users

options.name: Allow arbitrary HTTP request definitions
options.summary: Let administrators configure methods, headers, bodies and expressions.
tradeoffs: Creates unacceptable SSRF, secret exposure and arbitrary behavior risk

decision.summary: Evolve the existing Admin boundaries: persist controlled public-HTTPS content adapters and health, turn the existing Task persistence into the single clockin orchestration contract, expose thin authenticated APIs, replace current UI assets with native HTML/CSS/ES modules, and retain the existing single Admin process and external Worker request contract.
decision.rationale: This is the smallest architecture that meets console-managed providers, reliable progress, failure-only recovery and a complete UI redesign without duplicating TaskService, creating a second deployment stack, importing persistence into the browser or changing excluded platform adapters.

rejected_options.name: Patch hard-coded provider URLs and current page
rejected_options.reason: It does not meet the management, health, durable task or complete interaction redesign requirements.

rejected_options.name: Introduce a frontend framework and external queue
rejected_options.reason: It violates the approved framework-free, single-process operating model and scale assumptions.

rejected_options.name: Allow arbitrary HTTP request definitions
rejected_options.reason: It exceeds the template boundary and creates avoidable SSRF and secret risk.

rejected_options.name: Create a second task table or orchestration service beside TaskService
rejected_options.reason: The baseline already has persistence primitives; duplicating them would split progress and conflict control.

impact_scope: Admin SQLite schema and response schemas
Content retrieval and scheduler health probes
Clockin orchestration and Admin task APIs
Admin browser assets and internal routes
Secret handling, import/export and deployment documentation
constraints: Do not change ai.cqzuxia.com login, upload, home, sports or daily adapter behavior.
Content providers are public HTTPS GET only and every resolved address and redirect target must be validated.
The browser may depend only on authenticated Admin HTTP APIs, never SQLAlchemy or provider endpoints directly.
Routes remain thin; provider selection and task orchestration belong to services using independent AsyncSession instances for background work.
The existing Task persistence is evolved rather than duplicated, and only one pending or running clockin task may exist.
Only one Admin process may own APScheduler and in-process background tasks.
No production frontend framework, runtime CDN dependency or build step.
Existing user and Worker secrets stay server-side; empty sensitive updates preserve the stored value.
Rollout uses a fresh SQLite database plus legacy version 1.0 file import, not in-place migration.
verification: Validate architecture evidence and ADR schemas.
Run Python unit and API integration tests with mocked external HTTP.
Run JavaScript syntax checks, Node unit tests and Playwright desktop/mobile flows.
Validate and build Docker Compose, restart the container and verify health and database persistence.
Run live content-source probes separately without real clockin accounts.
rollback_or_migration: Use a fresh SQLite database for the new deployment and import a legacy version 1.0 configuration file.
Revert content, task, UI, security and deployment commits independently in reverse order.
Discard the candidate database and redeploy the previous Admin revision if rollout fails.
Never restore or reuse a leaked Worker token during rollback.
